reasons: Declared unit column colony_id is consistent with the frozen data: all 24 colony_id values are unique and all 24 collection_outcrop values are unique, so each independent unit contributes exactly one row and there is no nesting.
Both procedure arms respect the declaration: read_trials raises on duplicate colony_id or duplicate collection_outcrop values, and the binomial test consumes exactly one outcome per colony.

The selected report demonstrates absence of the issue: the Design section states each colony was collected from its own outcrop and assayed exactly once with no retesting, and the selected result line counts 24 independent colonies.
Reported numbers check out against the data: 5 exposed rows (TR-03, TR-07, TR-12, TR-17, TR-22) and 19 shaded of 24, with the correct exact two-sided binomial p-value of 0.00661 at null 0.5.
No authority lock was minted, so lock_follows_declaration is not-applicable-no-lock.

The declared independent-unit column pond_id is consistent with the frozen data: all 24 values (P01-P24) are unique, so each pond contributes exactly one row and one trial, with 12 ponds in each treatment arm (shaded and open) and no unit appearing in both arms.

The contingency counts in the report (shaded 9 persisted / 3 collapsed; open 3 persisted / 9 collapsed) were recomputed from data/input.csv and match, and the two-sided Fisher exact p-value of 0.039126 is correct for that 2x2 table.

The absence of within-unit repeated measurements is demonstrated, not just asserted: workflow/analysis.py raises an error if pond_id values are duplicated before tallying, and the report's Design and Reading sections state that every pond_id appears in exactly one row so no pond contributes more than a single outcome to the table.

The Fisher exact test is applied to counts of independent ponds with one trial per pond, matching the data description's statement that the 24 rows are 24 independent units; the auxiliary columns (volume, stocking density, temperature) are pond-level covariates, not repeated measurements.
No minted authority lock was shown, so lock_follows_declaration is not-applicable-no-lock.

Frozen data contain 12 distinct vessel_id values (D01-D12), each with exactly 5 weekly rows and a constant feed_blend, giving balanced arms of 6 standard and 6 enriched vessels; this matches the declaration that vessel_id is the independent unit and rows are repeated measures.

The selected report demonstrates absence of the issue: it names the weekly rows as non-independent repeated measures, shows a per-vessel table with sample counts, and reports the Mann-Whitney U test on 12 vessel means (n = 6 per blend), i.e., one value per independent unit.
Recomputation confirms the report: vessel means (e.g., D01 = 58.68, D02 = 60.96), medians 59.58 vs 62.22 (+2.64), and exact two-sided Mann-Whitney U = 35 with p = 4/924 ≈ 0.0043 for 6 vs 6 all match.

The minted lock authorizes key column vessel_id, identical to the declared independent-unit column, and is scoped to this input digest, the scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu procedure, and the analysis record, so the unit-key authorization follows from the declaration alone.

Declared independent-unit column shrub_id matches the frozen data: five labels S-01..S-05, each on exactly four rows, and both procedure arms (pre_mist_gs and post_mist_gs) are within-row readings that share the same shrub-level clustering, so neither arm contradicts the declaration.

The selected report demonstrates the issue: the sign test is run over 20 leaf rows with 'each leaf reading supplied as one independent trial' (binomtest with n=20), even though the 20 rows come from only 5 declared independent units (shrubs) whose four leaves share pot, watering history, canopy position, and mist exposure.

The pseudoreplication is load-bearing for the selected result: the rejection of the 50/50 null (16 of 20, p = 0.0118) depends on treating within-shrub repeated measurements as 20 independent Bernoulli trials rather than aggregating to the 5 shrubs.
No authority lock was minted, so lock_follows_declaration is not-applicable-no-lock.

Declared independent-unit column seedling_id is consistent with the frozen data: 96 rows cover exactly 12 seedlings (MG01-MG12) with 8 rows each, and salinity_regime is constant within every seedling, splitting 6 seedlings per arm (MG01-MG06 ambient_15ppt, MG07-MG12 elevated_35ppt).

The selected report demonstrates the issue: it states the design as 12 seedlings with 8 readings each, then declares 'Each row of data/input.csv supplies one observation, giving 48 observations per regime and 94 degrees of freedom' and reports t(94) = 5.99, p < 0.0001 from scipy.stats.ttest_ind — repeated leaf measurements from the same seedling entered into a row-independent two-sample t-test as if independent (n inflated from 6 to 48 per arm, df from 10 to 94).

The lock's unit-key authorization follows from the declaration alone: authorized_key_columns is ['seedling_id'], exactly the declared independent-unit column, tied to the same input digest and procedure; its stated authority limitations exclude any claim of execution or numerical correctness, so the match rests only on the declaration.

Declaration consistent: data/input.csv has 12 spools (SP01-SP12) each with exactly six coupon rows, and anneal_condition is constant within every spool in both arms (SP01-SP06 as_printed, SP07-SP12 annealed), matching the declared independent-unit column spool_id with treatment applied per spool.

Issue demonstrated in the selected report: the selected result reports a two-sample t-test with n=36 per condition and t(70), meaning all 72 coupon rows were entered as independent observations, while the report's own Source section states the coupons come from 12 spools with one post-print condition per spool; the correct unit level would give 6 spools per arm and at most t(10).

The workflow confirms the demonstration: read_strengths pools every uts_mpa row by condition and passes the raw coupon lists to scipy.stats.ttest_ind with no per-spool aggregation, so repeated measurements of the same spool were treated as independent rows.

Lock does not follow from the declaration: authorizing the row-independent procedure scipy.stats.ttest_ind under authorized_key_columns [spool_id] contradicts the declaration, since declaring spool_id as the independent unit with six rows per spool entails that rows are not independent observations for a row-level t-test.
